title: Coefficient-isomorphism transport of compactification functors and their adjoints
statement:
Let $\Lambda,\Lambda'$ be commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $e:\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda'$ a ring-object isomorphism. Use small pro-étale sites in one fixed universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $T$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, $\Lambda'_T=p_T^*\Lambda'$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], let
$$U_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda')$$
be termwise restriction of scalars along $p_T^*(e^{-1})$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal C'_T=\Dctf(T,\Lambda')$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $\mathcal L_T$ (respectively $\mathcal L'_T$) be the intersection of all full replete triangulated subcategories of the corresponding ambient derived category containing $\mathcal C_T$ (respectively $\mathcal C'_T$) and closed under ambient small coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with a fixed compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow Z,p:Z\to Y)$, where $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $p$ is proper and $pj=f$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Write $H_\Lambda=Rp_{*,\Lambda}D(j_{!,\Lambda})$ and $H_{\Lambda'}=Rp_{*,\Lambda'}D(j_{!,\Lambda'})$ with the pulled-back module-object convention [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek].

Each $U_T$ is an exact equivalence preserving all small coproducts, identifies $\mathcal C_T$ with $\mathcal C'_T$, and restricts to an exact equivalence $\mathcal L_T\simeq\mathcal L'_T$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$U_YH_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{\Lambda'}U_X.$$
If $H_\Lambda$ carries $\mathcal L_X$ into $\mathcal L_Y$, then $H_{\Lambda'}$ carries $\mathcal L'_X$ into $\mathcal L'_Y$; write $F_\Lambda,F_{\Lambda'}$ for these restrictions. Suppose adjunctions $F_\Lambda\dashv G_\Lambda$ and $F_{\Lambda'}\dashv G_{\Lambda'}$ are given, with counits $\varepsilon_\Lambda,\varepsilon_{\Lambda'}$. The left comparison $a:U_YF_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}U_X$ has a unique counit-compatible right comparison
$$b:U_XG_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\Lambda'}U_Y,$$
characterized, for $N\in\mathcal L_Y$, by
$$\varepsilon_{\Lambda',U_YN}\circ F_{\Lambda'}(b_N)\circ a_{G_\Lambda N}=U_Y(\varepsilon_{\Lambda,N}).$$
In particular $G_\Lambda(\mathcal C_Y)\subseteq\mathcal C_X$ if and only if $G_{\Lambda'}(\mathcal C'_Y)\subseteq\mathcal C'_X$.

proof.text: Use the existing sheaf tensor, Grothendieck sheaf, and module-object instances to supply the ambient abelian and closed monoidal structures. The preservation statement needs no separate construction of coproducts: an equivalence preserves every existing small coproduct, including the empty one.

source.place: Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products, assertions (1)-(2); module-object hypothesis supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text: Put $r_T=p_T^*(e^{-1}):\Lambda'_T\to\Lambda_T$ and $s_T=p_T^*e$. Functoriality of pulled-back ring objects gives $r_Ts_T=1$ and $s_Tr_T=1$. Restriction along $r_T$ and $s_T$ therefore gives inverse additive exact equivalences of module categories by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; the required closedness, equalizers and coequalizers were supplied in step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to both functors. The resulting triangulated functors are $U_T$ and $V_T=D(\operatorname{Res}_{s_T})$. Their two composites are naturally the identity: on complexes their actions and differentials are unchanged after the two scalar restrictions, and these identities descend through localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $U_T$ is an exact equivalence with inverse $V_T$.

proof.text: The equivalence $U_T$ preserves all ambient small coproducts, by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] applied to its derived equivalence; the same is true of $V_T$. For constructibility apply [lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible] to $e$ and then to $e^{-1}$. It gives $U_T(\mathcal C_T)\subseteq\mathcal C'_T$ and $V_T(\mathcal C'_T)\subseteq\mathcal C_T$. Since the two composites are isomorphic to the identity and these full subcategories are replete, $U_T$ identifies $\mathcal C_T$ with $\mathcal C'_T$. This uses exactly finite constant local models and finite Tor amplitude of the item, with no admissibility or finite-type hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text: Consider the full replete class $\mathcal S_T=\{M:U_TM\in\mathcal L'_T\}$ in the unprimed ambient category. It contains $\mathcal C_T$ by step 3. It is triangulated because $U_T$ is exact, and closed under small coproducts because $U_T$ preserves them. The defining intersection for $\mathcal L_T$ therefore gives $\mathcal L_T\subseteq\mathcal S_T$, that is, $U_T\mathcal L_T\subseteq\mathcal L'_T$. Interchanging $U_T,V_T$ gives $V_T\mathcal L'_T\subseteq\mathcal L_T$. The inverse isomorphisms then restrict to these full replete subcategories. They give the asserted exact equivalence $\mathcal L_T\simeq\mathcal L'_T$: their shifts and distinguished triangles are the ambient ones by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text:
Apply [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] to $r_T$. It identifies $\operatorname{Ext}_{r_T}$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{s_T}$, which is exact by step 2. Thus extension of scalars along the condensed ring morphism $e^{-1}:\Lambda'\to\Lambda$ preserves finite limits on every scheme, exactly the flatness hypothesis in [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso]. Apply that node to $e^{-1}$ and $p:Z\to Y$, with the roles of $\Lambda,\Lambda'$ interchanged. The resulting canonical natural isomorphism is
$$d:U_YRp_{*,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,\Lambda'}U_Z.$$
In particular this comparison is on the ordinary unbounded categories; no bounded-below reduction or finite cohomological dimension is used.

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text:
Apply [def-sfb-comap-open-immersion-shriek-iso] to the same $e^{-1}$ and to $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$. It gives $\operatorname{Res}_{r_Z}j_{!,\Lambda}\cong j_{!,\Lambda'}\operatorname{Res}_{r_X}$. All functors in this square are exact: scalar restriction by step 2, and $j_!$ by the module-derived-lower-shriek convention. Applying the isomorphism termwise to complexes and then localizing gives
$$h:U_ZD(j_{!,\Lambda})\xrightarrow{\sim}D(j_{!,\Lambda'})U_X.$$
Whisker $d$ by $D(j_{!,\Lambda})$ and $h$ by $Rp_{*,\Lambda'}$. Their composite is
$$U_YRp_{*,\Lambda}D(j_{!,\Lambda})\xrightarrow{d}Rp_{*,\Lambda'}U_ZD(j_{!,\Lambda})\xrightarrow{Rp_{*,\Lambda'}h}Rp_{*,\Lambda'}D(j_{!,\Lambda'})U_X.$$
By the definition of $H$ this is the requested canonical $U_YH_\Lambda\cong H_{\Lambda'}U_X$.

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text: Suppose $H_\Lambda(\mathcal L_X)\subseteq\mathcal L_Y$, and let $M'\in\mathcal L'_X$. Step 4 gives $V_XM'\in\mathcal L_X$. Hence $H_\Lambda V_XM'\in\mathcal L_Y$ and $U_YH_\Lambda V_XM'\in\mathcal L'_Y$. Step 6 and $U_XV_XM'\cong M'$ identify this last object with $H_{\Lambda'}M'$. Repleteness proves $H_{\Lambda'}(\mathcal L'_X)\subseteq\mathcal L'_Y$. The ambient comparison therefore restricts to $a:U_YF_\Lambda\cong F_{\Lambda'}U_X$ on the full subcategories. The restrictions of $U_X,U_Y$ are those of step 4.

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text:
For brevity write $F=F_\Lambda$, $F'=F_{\Lambda'}$, $G=G_\Lambda$, $G'=G_{\Lambda'}$, and $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'$ for the given counits; write $\eta'$ for the unit of $F'\dashv G'$. For $N\in\mathcal L_Y$ put
$$t_N=U_Y(\varepsilon_N)\circ a_{GN}^{-1}:F'U_XGN\longrightarrow U_YN,$$
$$b_N=G'(t_N)\circ\eta'_{U_XGN}:U_XGN\longrightarrow G'U_YN.$$
Naturality of $a,\varepsilon,\eta'$ makes $b$ natural. This is precisely the mate formula of [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $L=F$, $R=G$, $L'=F'$, $R'=G'$, the vertical functors $U_X,U_Y$, and $\theta=a^{-1}$. Step 4 makes $U_X$ an equivalence and $U_Y$ fully faithful, so that node proves that $b$ is a natural isomorphism. In particular we use the given adjunctions, without choosing new ones.

source.place: Ring-isomorphism specialization of the coefficient comparisons; explicit argument written by NV.

proof.text:
For the adjunction $F'\dashv G'$, the hom-bijection formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] say that $b_N$ just defined is the adjunct of $t_N$, and therefore
$$\varepsilon'_{U_YN}\circ F'(b_N)=t_N.$$
Composing with $a_{GN}$ gives exactly
$$\varepsilon'_{U_YN}\circ F'(b_N)\circ a_{GN}=U_Y(\varepsilon_N).$$
Conversely any component $c_N$ satisfying this identity obeys $\varepsilon'_{U_YN}\circ F'(c_N)=t_N$ after composition with $a_{GN}^{-1}$. Injectivity of the same adjunction bijection gives $c_N=b_N$. Thus the counit equation determines every component and hence determines the natural comparison uniquely.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following adjunction-map formulas; specialize the bijection to t_N.

proof.text: If $G(\mathcal C_Y)\subseteq\mathcal C_X$, let $N'\in\mathcal C'_Y$. Step 3 gives $V_YN'\in\mathcal C_Y$, so $G V_YN'\in\mathcal C_X$ and $U_XG V_YN'\in\mathcal C'_X$. The component $b_{V_YN'}$ and $U_YV_YN'\cong N'$ identify this object with $G'N'$, proving the primed inclusion. Conversely, for $N\in\mathcal C_Y$ the primed inclusion gives $G'U_YN\in\mathcal C'_X$. The isomorphism $b_N$ then puts $U_XGN$ in $\mathcal C'_X$. Applying $V_X$, step 3 and $V_XU_XGN\cong GN$ put $GN$ in $\mathcal C_X$. This proves the claimed equivalence of restrictions.
